# Scatterplots
We've already been introduced to many scatterplots! We've used a scatterplot to generate a linear calibration curve: 
```{r cal curve}
#You may have to change your working directory here! I saved all my workbooks and data in a specific folder called "ethyl carbamate", so I have to specify that in the file name.  
calibration <- read.csv("EC_calibration.csv")

#I'm removing the data we removed before
calibration[which(calibration$fluor_signal_area == 220.5), 'fluor_signal_area'] <- NA
calibration[which(calibration$conc > 40), 'ms_signalintensity'] <- NA
calibration[which(calibration$ms_signalintensity == 4009), 'ms_signalintensity'] <- NA

HPLC <- ggplot(calibration , aes(conc_ug_L, fluor_signal_area)) + 
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  labs(title = "Final HPLC Calibration Curve",
       x = "concentration of ethyl carbamide (\u00B5g/L)",
       y = "fluorescence (au)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)+
  ylim(0,800)+
  xlim(5,50)

GC <- ggplot(calibration , aes(conc_ug_L, ms_signalintensity)) + 
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  labs(title = "Final GC Calibration Curve",
       x = "concentration of ethyl carbamide (\u00B5g/L)",
       y = "signal intensity (counts)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)+
  xlim(0,40)+
  ylim(0,10000)

calplots <- plot_grid(HPLC, GC)

calplots

#This is how you save a plot to insert into other work!

ggsave( "CalCurves.png", plot = calplots, dpi = 500, height = 4, width = 8, units = "in")
```

Dual axis scatterplots
```{r dual axis}

coeff <- 30
dual <- ggplot(calibration , aes(conc_ug_L, ms_signalintensity )) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "blue")+
  geom_point(aes(conc_ug_L, fluor_signal_area*coeff), size = 3, colour = "red")+
  labs(title = "All Calibration Curves",
       x = "concentration of ethyl carbamide (\u00B5g/L)",
       y = "signal intensity (counts)") +
  theme_bw()+
  xlim(0,40)+
  ylim(0,10000)+
  scale_y_continuous(
    
    # Features of the first axis
    name = "signal intensity (counts)",
    
    # Add a second axis and specify its features
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~./coeff, name="fluorescence (au)")
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = "red"), 
        axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = "blue"), 
        axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = "blue"), 
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = "red"))

dual
```

To discuss overplotting, we first have to import the ozone data we used previously.
```{r ozone import}

##Here is the code we used to import the ozone data. You will have to specify your working directory!

OzoneData <- read_csv("OzoneData.csv", skip = 28, name_repair ="minimal") 

colnames(OzoneData)[1:10] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[1:10], "_O3_Leth")

colnames(OzoneData)[11:20] <-  sub(".1", "", colnames(OzoneData)[11:20])
colnames(OzoneData)[11:20] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[11:20], "_CO_Leth")

colnames(OzoneData)[21:30] <-  sub(".2", "", colnames(OzoneData)[21:30])
colnames(OzoneData)[21:30] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[21:30], "_O3_Calgary")

colnames(OzoneData)[31:40] <-  sub(".3", "", colnames(OzoneData)[31:40])
colnames(OzoneData)[31:40] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[31:40], "_CO_Calgary")

colnames(OzoneData)[41:50] <-  sub(".4", "", colnames(OzoneData)[41:50])
colnames(OzoneData)[41:50] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[41:50], "_O3_Edmonton")

colnames(OzoneData)[51:60] <-  sub(".5", "", colnames(OzoneData)[51:60])
colnames(OzoneData)[51:60] <- paste0(colnames(OzoneData)[51:60], "_CO_Edmonton")

OzoneData <- OzoneData %>%
  select(contains(c("Start", "Measurement", "Flags"))) %>%
  mutate(`Measurement Value_O3_Leth` = `Measurement Value_O3_Leth`*1000)

OzoneData <- OzoneData %>%
  mutate(date = as.POSIXct(`Interval Start_O3_Leth`, tz = "MST", format = "%Y-%m-%j %H:%M")) %>%
  select(!contains("Interval Start"))

OzoneDataLong <- OzoneData %>%
  select(!contains("Flags"))%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Measurement Value"), 
               names_to = c("pollutant", "location"),
               names_pattern = "Measurement Value_(.*)_(.*)",
               values_to = "measurements")
```


```{r overplot}
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")),
  aes(x= Hour, y = measurements))+
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Initial Plot")

Leth

#Solution 2 - sampling points

Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H"))%>%
  sample_frac(0.10) ,
  aes(x= Hour, y = measurements))+
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Sampling Solution")

Leth

#Solution 3 - transparency
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")),
  aes(x= Hour, y = measurements))+
  geom_point(colour = "purple", alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Transparency Solution")

Leth

#Solution 4 - density
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")),
  aes(x= Hour, y = measurements) ) +
  geom_bin2d(binwidth = c(1, 1)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +  # High-contrast color palette
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "2D Solution", fill = "Count")

Leth

#Solution 5: jittering
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")),
  aes(x= Hour, y = measurements))+
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2) +
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Jittering")

Leth
```
When should we plot with lines vs points? Lines can help visualize data that is known to be linked together! For example time!
```{r lines}
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneData, aes(x = date, y = `Measurement Value_O3_Leth`))+
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw()+
  ggtitle("Lethbridge")
Leth

Leth <- ggplot(OzoneData, aes(x = date, y = `Measurement Value_O3_Leth`))+
  geom_line() + 
  theme_bw()+
  ggtitle("Lethbridge")

Leth

# Great for data exploration!
ggplotly(Leth)
```

```{r barplot}
O3_summary <- OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")) %>%
  group_by(Hour) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(measurements, na.rm = TRUE), 
            sd = sd(measurements, na.rm = TRUE))
         
         
Leth <- ggplot(O3_summary,
  aes(x= Hour, y = mean))+
  geom_col() +
  theme_bw()+
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd), 
    width = 0.2, 
    color = "black", 
    size = 1
  ) +
  labs(title = "Bar Plot")

Leth

```

```{r boxplot}


Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")) %>%
  group_by(Hour),
  aes(x = Hour, y = measurements)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.color = "red", outlier.shape = 16) 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

Leth

#Combining with jitter!
  
Leth <- ggplot(OzoneDataLong %>%
  filter(location == "Leth", pollutant == "O3") %>%
  mutate(Hour = format(as.POSIXct(date), "%H")) %>%
  group_by(Hour),
  aes(x = Hour, y = measurements)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.2, size = 1)+
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.color = "red", outlier.shape = 16)
  
Leth

```
